topic.name: Solving Quadratic Equations with No Constant Term

question.explanation:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor:

\begin{align*} 6w^2+ 3w -5&=2w^2- 5\\[5pt] 6w^2+ 3w -5 -(2w^2- 5) &=0\\[5pt] 6w^2+ 3w -5 - 2w^2 + 5 &=0\\[5pt] (6w^2 - 2w^2)+3w+ (-5 +5)&= 0\\[5pt] 4w^2 + 3w &= 0 \\[5pt] w(4w + 3) &= 0 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get \[ w=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad 4w + 3 =0, \] which in turn gives \[ w=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad w=-\dfrac{3}{4}. \]

Therefore, the solutions are $w=-\dfrac{3}{4}, 0.$

example.title: Solving When Both Sides are Quadratic

question.text: In ascending order, the solutions to $\dfrac{1}{5}t^2 = -3t$ are $t=$
question.explanation:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{1}{5}t^2 &= -3t \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{5}t^2 + 3t &= 0 \\[5pt] %\dfrac{1}{5}\left(t^2 + 15t\right) &= 0 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{5}t\left(t+15\right) &= 0 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get \[ \dfrac{1}{5}t = 0 \qquad \textrm{or}\qquad t+15 = 0, \] which in turn gives \[ t = 0 \qquad \textrm{or}\qquad t=-15. \]

Therefore, the solutions are $t=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-15}$ and $t= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}.$

example.title: Solving When the Right-Hand Side Is Not Zero

question.text: In ascending order, the solutions to $4g^2 = \dfrac{2g}{5}$ are $g=$
question.explanation:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor: \begin{align*} 4g^2 &= \dfrac{2g}{5} \\[3pt] 4g^2 - \dfrac{2g}{5} & = 0 \\[3pt] 2g\left(2g - \dfrac 15 \right) &= 0 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get \[ 2g = 0 \qquad \textrm{or}\qquad 2g - \dfrac 15 = 0, \] which in turn gives \[ g = 0 \qquad \textrm{or}\qquad g = \dfrac {1}{10}. \]

Therefore, the solutions are $g=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}$ and $g= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{10}}.$
